svg.aria-label: Three ways to get RViz pixels from the Linux dev container onto the screen of the host: X11 forwarding to XQuartz, a VNC server in the container viewed in a browser through noVNC, and a headless Xvfb display captured to a PNG file. In every route the 3D rendering happens inside the container with the llvmpipe software rasteriser, because Docker Desktop exposes no GPU to it.

g.text: Getting RViz onto the screen of the host
dev container — Ubuntu 24.04, ROS 2 Jazzy
rviz2 · joint_state_publisher_gui
Qt 5 widgets + an Ogre 3D viewport
Mesa llvmpipe
software OpenGL 4.5, on the CPU
already in the image: libgl1-mesa-dri
there is no GPU to reach for
Docker Desktop runs Linux in a VM and
passes no graphics device through, so any
GPU the host may have is never used
what this costs
Every triangle is drawn by the CPU. The
hexapod is a small model, so it is usable;
keep the RViz window modest, leave the
TF display off, and give Docker Desktop
4 CPUs or more.
three ways out of the container
1 · X11 to XQuartz
DISPLAY=host.docker.internal:0 — RViz appears as an ordinary host window.
Changes: swap DISPLAY in devcontainer.json. Nothing to add to the image.
Needs an X server on the host: XQuartz on macOS, WSLg on Windows, none on Linux.
whole framebuffer travels over TCP — the heaviest of the three
2 · noVNC in a browser — what this workspace ships
Xvfb + x11vnc + websockify inside the container; open http://localhost:6080
Already set up: scripts/start-gui.sh, run by the devcontainer postStartCommand.
Needs: nothing on the host. Any modern browser is the whole client.
only changed rectangles cross the boundary, and they are compressed
survives a Docker Desktop restart of the network better than an X socket does
3 · headless capture
Xvfb only, then `import -window root shot.png`. No viewer at all.
Uses the same packages as route 2. Nothing interactive.
Needs: nothing. This is how the screenshots in this document were made.
for a scripted check that the model still loads, not for driving the robot
